paragraphs.text: Heb. In waiting I waited; Diutissime quidem, sed optimo successu; I prayed and waited, I waited and prayed again; persevering in prayer, and begging audience, as Psa 39:12, with which Basil maketh this psalm to cohere; and well he may, for it seemeth to be of the same time and argument with the two former. Est sensus eiusdem cum duobus prioribus. R. Obadiah saith, that David composed this psalm after that he was recovered of his leprosy, Psa 38:7.
paragraphs.anchor: I waited patiently for the Lord

paragraphs.text: i.e. He began at length to show favour; for he waiteth to be gracious, and well knoweth that desideria dilatione crescant, et cito data vilescant; nothing is lost by holding his people long in request.
paragraphs.anchor: And he inclined unto me

paragraphs.text: E puteo sonitus, ut Isa 51:14, out of a noiseful pit, where there is a continual hurry by the great tall of waters into it: he meaneth out of dreadful dangers, out of a desperate disease, saith R. Obadiah; who also by rock here understandeth perfect health, Sanitatem in corpore, sanctitatem in corde.
paragraphs.anchor: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit

paragraphs.text: E luto, luto, saith Kimchi, for here are two words used of one and the same sense; to show that, as a bemired beast, he was in a perishing condition till God pulled him out, and set him on firm ground.
paragraphs.anchor: Out of the miry clay

paragraphs.text: That I might not relapse into the same or fall into another malady or mischief.
paragraphs.anchor: And established my goings

paragraphs.text: i.e. New matter, which I shall soon contrive into a new song, by the help of his Holy Spirit; for I cannot breathe out a desire after him except he first give me breath therewith, and so put a new song in my mouth.
paragraphs.anchor: And he hath put a new song in my mouth

paragraphs.text: i.e. Unto Christ, saith Junius, to whom and of whom the Church singeth, saith he, in the following verses.
paragraphs.anchor: Even praise unto our God

paragraphs.text: Their eye shall affect their heart, both with fear of and faith in the Lord, that bringeth greatest things to pass, and is fearful in praises, doing wonders, Exo 15:11.
paragraphs.anchor: Many shall see it, and fear, and trust in the Lord

paragraphs.text: See Psa 2:12.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed is that man, &c.

paragraphs.text: Who are set in opposition to believers, as they are also, Hab 2:4. Self-justitiaries especially, and meritmongers: faith is a humbling grace.
paragraphs.anchor: And respecteth not the proud

paragraphs.text: As do heretics and idolaters. These the true believer, out of the greatness of his spirit, slighteth, how great soever they be; animo magno nihil magnum.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor such as turn aside to lies

paragraphs.text: Many and great, and all for them that trust in thee; who therefore must needs be blessed, as Psa 40:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Many, O Lord my God, are thy works which thou hast done

paragraphs.text: Thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give us an expected end, Jer 29:11.
paragraphs.anchor: And thy thoughts which are to us-ward

paragraphs.text: No, nor yet out of order; and yet we must be reckoning and relating them as we are able, to God, and men, by speaking good of his name; and at this David was old excellent, as we say.
paragraphs.anchor: They cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee

paragraphs.text: By wholesale we must do it, though we cannot so well by retail; particulars also must be instanced, as Moses doth to Jethro, Exo 18:7-8, and for that end catalogues must be kept. See one Jdg 10:11-12.
paragraphs.anchor: If I should declare and speak of them

paragraphs.text: Comparatively to the obedience of faith, 1Sa 15:22, without which, when hypocrites thought to bribe God by cold ceremonies, they were rejected.
paragraphs.anchor: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire

paragraphs.text: Christ is the end of the law to all that believe; that Lamb of God, slain from the beginning of the world, is the only expiatory sacrifice, and the foundation of that fore-mentioned blessedness, Psa 40:4. Now, since Christ suffered, the Levitical sacrifices being abolished, we have none to offer but such as are gratulatory, to show our thankfulness for such a Redeemer, whose perfect obedience, with the fruit of it, is here and in the following verses both described, and set forth for an absolute pattern to us of performing our duty toward God, for this inexplicable mercy.

Confer Heb 10:5-6, &c. Here we have in Christ for our instruction, and in David also (his type) for our example, 1. A firm purpose of obedience, in a bored ear add a yielding heart. 2. A ready performance thereof, "Lo, I come." 3. A carefull observance of the word written, "In the volume of thy book it is written of me," Psa 40:7 4. A hearty delight in that observance, Psa 40:8 5. A public profession and communication of God’s goodness to others, Psa 40:9-10 (D. Ames). Now, we should labour to express Christ to the world, to walk as he walked, 1Jn 2:6; our lives should be in some sense parallel with his life, as the transcript with the original. He left us a copy to write by, saith St Peter, 1Pe 2:21

Heb. digged, bored; a hearing ear hast thou bestowed upon me, which is a singular favour; for life entereth by the ear, Isa 55:3, as did death at first, Gen 3:19 Oh, pray that God would make the bore wide enough; that the inward ears being drawn up to the outward, one sound may pierce both at once.
paragraphs.anchor: Mine ears hast thou opened

paragraphs.text: Christ became obedient even to the death, yea, that of the cross, Php 2:8. Christ’s people also are a willing people, Psa 110:3, their obedience is prompt and present, ready and speedy, without delays and consults, Psa 119:60, without capitulation and security, Isa 56:6.
paragraphs.anchor: Then said I, Lo, I come

paragraphs.text: In libro plicatili, in thy law, which was anciently (and is still this day among the Jews) written in paper or parchment rolled up; because it will last longer rolled than folded.
paragraphs.anchor: In the volume of the book

paragraphs.text: Of Christ, in many places; for he is both author, object, matter, and mark of both Testaments. Of David also, and all God’s people, doth the law speak with fruit and efficacy; and they do use to read their own names, written, as it were, in every precept, promise, threatening. Look how men read the statute book of the land, as holding themselves highly concerned therein: so here.
paragraphs.anchor: It is written of me

paragraphs.text: To Christ it was his meat and drink, Joh 4:34, he set his face to do it, and to suffer it, Luk 9:51; yea, he was straitened, pained, till it was done, Luk 12:50. And the same mind is also in the saints that was in Christ Jesus, Php 2:5. They delight in the law of God after the inward man, Rom 7:22, they prefer it before their necessary food, Job 23:12.
paragraphs.anchor: I delight to do thy will, O my God

paragraphs.text: Heb. in the midst of my bowels; there is the counterpane, the duplicate of the law written, yea, printed, Jer 31:33 2Co 3:3. Rip up my heart (said Queen Mary) when I am dead, and there shall you find Calais, the loss whereof (it is thought) killed her. Rip up the most men’s hearts, and there you shall find written, The god of this present world. But God’s law is in good men’s hearts, to live and to die with it: O beata Apocalypsis (said that martyr, catching up that revelation cast into the same fire with him to be burnt), O blessed revelation, how happy am I to be burned with thee in my hands!
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, thy law is within my heart

paragraphs.text: David did this, but Christ much more, by the everlasting gospel, sent the whole world throughout. Great was the company of preachers, and large was their commission. See a draught of it Act 26:18.
paragraphs.anchor: I have preached righteousness in the great congregation

paragraphs.text: Righteousness of Christ imputed, faithfulness of God in fulfilling his promises, salvation the end of faith, lovingkindness and truth the ground of all the former, God’s lovingkindness, or mercy moving him to promise, and his truth binding him to perform; these are those pearls that Christ by his preachers casteth before people, if they be but as forward to take them as he is to tender them. How beautiful should the feet be of those that bring such glad tidings! and how heavy will the dust of such feet be, shaken off against despisers!
paragraphs.anchor: I have declared thy faithfulness, and thy salvation

paragraphs.text: sc. That I have herein done mine utmost, and with an upright heart.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord, thou knowest

paragraphs.text: Or, if he did, as Psa 119:11, it was, that having wrought it first on his own affections, he might afterwards utter it a corde ad cor, from the heart to the heart, and so be able to save himself and those that heard him.
paragraphs.anchor: I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart

paragraphs.text: See Psa 40:9.
paragraphs.anchor: I have declared thy faithfulness, &c.

paragraphs.text: Whereas, while the saints are on earth there will be a perpetual interchange of comforts and crosses; prayers must be joined with praises, and care taken that, confirmed by former experiences, they still depend upon God. Nunc in luto adhuc haerens et cum residuo calamitatum colluctans precatur Deum.
paragraphs.anchor: Withhold not thou thy tender mercies, &c.

paragraphs.text: Tuos illos custodes mihi ad latus adhibe, let those two attributes of thine be mine angel guardians at all times. {See Trapp on "Psa 25:10"}
paragraphs.anchor: Let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me

paragraphs.text: Heb. have mustered upon me. Many (or millions) are the troubles of the righteous; none out of hell ever suffered more than they: an elegant exaggeration of their afflictions we have in this verse, and such as cannot well be understood by any but those that have been wellbeaten porters to the cross of Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: For innumerable evils have compassed me

paragraphs.text: i.e. The punishment of mine iniquities, Gen 4:13, my sin hath found me out. If this be taken of Christ, he is Maximus peccatorum, the greatest of sinners by imputation, 2Co 5:20 Isa 53:6, for our sins (which here he calleth his) he suffered; and here his bitter agony in the garden is graphically described; neither is it absurd to say, that as he bore our sins in his own body upon the tree, he was first redeemed by himself, and afterwards we.
paragraphs.anchor: Mine iniquities have taken hold upon me

paragraphs.text: i.e. My wit, courage, counsel is wasted by earnest thinking upon them. Scientia mea eis numerandis deficit, as Kimchi glosseth.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore my heart faileth me

paragraphs.text: Do it of thy free grace, and mere mercy of thy good will and gracious liking (as the word ευδοκια signifieth), beside the consideration of my woeful misery laid forth, Psa 40:12, as an object of thy mercy.
paragraphs.anchor: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me

paragraphs.text: These and the like imprecations must be looked upon as prophecies. Besides, David looked upon them not as his enemies only, but God’s as well; and such also as were desperate and irrecoverable. So Paul prayed against the coppersmith, the Church against Julian, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them be ashamed and confounded together, &c.

paragraphs.text: A Christian may without sin be sensible of indignities; only it must be the mourning of doves, and not the roaring of bears.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them be driven backward, &c.

paragraphs.text: A poor reward; but such as sin payeth to her servants: "the wages of sin is death." Sin payeth all her servants in black money. See Psa 35:21. The word here rendered reward signifieth a heel. It is as if the prophet should say, Let one desolation tread upon the heels of another, till they be utterly undone.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them be desolate for a reward

paragraphs.text: viz. When they hear of my deliverance. The saints have both their joys and griefs in common with their fellow members, as being in the body, Heb 13:3; both in the body of Christ and in the body of flesh and frailty.
paragraphs.anchor: Let all those that seek thee rejoice

paragraphs.text: A stark beggar neither will I hide from my Lord (as once Joseph’s brethren said to him, when they came for corn) mine extreme indigence, my necessitous condition; I am one that get my living by begging.
paragraphs.anchor: But I am poor and needy

paragraphs.text: He is the poor man’s King, as hath been said; and Christ is cum Patre dator, inter nos petitor, as Augustine hath it; that is, he gives with the Father, and at the same time prays with the suitor, who must therefore needs speed.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet the Lord thinketh upon me

paragraphs.text: Deliver me speedily, lest I perish utterly. God, saith one, is sometimes troubled with too much help, but never with too little; we are sometimes too soon, but he is never too late.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying
